awry: Why, she wondered, should one’s physical properties always insist upon appearing awry after a night of stolen or forbidden pleasure?
They need it to right the balance of a world sadly awry because of its brutal neglect of the rights of women and children.

Of course throw monstrous shadows: those who think
Awry, will scarce act straightly. Who but he?
And who but you can wonder? He has been mad,

The women and the men of garish nights,
Their eyes wine-weakened and their clothes awry,
Grotesques beneath the strong electric lights.

Squeaked in the floor, long after it was gone
Her flesh would sit awry on her. By day
She would forget somewhat, and it would seem
I had my face turned from you, therefore I read the letters awry and knew not their meaning.
